I'm seriously considering buying a handgun in the immediate future. I've wanted one for a long time and am now in a place of financial stability that I feel I can spend the money on an expensive item I consider a bit of a luxury. As such I would like to get the opinions of my fellow voaters on the gun manufacturers I would be interested in. I've never even seen Sig Sauer mentioned on voat before and I'm curious of the general opinion towards them. The reason I would be interested in buying a Sig would primarily be that it is the preferred brand of handgun for a few different fictional characters in novels I've read. I admit it's a lame reason, but I have nothing better and there are almost certainly worse.

I'm still in the advanced planning stages of my purchase, a lot more preparation and research needs to be done before I go through with it. Not the least of which is tracking down and taking a gun safety course. And buying a gun safe or similarly secure storage device before I even apply for a permit to purchase the gun.

You're on the right path - take your course, and try as many different guns as you can. What you think you'll like, and what you later discover that you like, are often different.

Sigs are fine pistols with a strong following. My own defensive gun is a Sig P250. However, the guns thats best for you is the one that fits your hands, has an action style that seems intuitive, and that you shoot well.

You've acknowledged how you interpret the purchase (luxury). Next step is to decide how you will be using it most of the time. I believe that answer would most inform your decision on brand. You deprecate your reason for getting a Sig, but you don't need to. You have a connection to it, and that will increase the satisfaction you get from it.

Regarding Sig: they make competition weapons. That's their primary mission. They certainly do make tactical arms, and they're fine weapons. So, if this is something you're mostly just taking to the range, they're a boatload of fun.

/u/Kromulent would probably disagree with me on this next point, but it's a personal bias. I would not choose a Sig for a carry weapon. I've seen them (Sig handguns, anyway) taken apart, and they tend to have a lot of moving parts, with very low tolerances (very little space between moving parts) - that's what makes them so smooth and tight. But, that's also a mark against reliability IMO.

I swear by Ruger. This is Olivia, my carry weapon. Not nearly as tight or clean as a Sig, but that's why I bought it. So, once again, we come back to your main use for it.

For a range gun, you really can't beat a Sig. Take care of it, and it will take care of you.
I absolutely love my P226 (.40 caliber). You can't go wrong with SIG except for the pricetag!

Although SiG made their name with massive service pistols P210 and P226, I never cared for their big-boy, professional offerings. I like P238 and P290.

Kromulent's P250 was a technologically groundbreaking gun with its chassis systems. Of course now even Ruger American comes on a chassis, but it was an amazing innovation back then So there's that. But always P250 looked like a tadpole to me.

The only time I read a book where a character carried SiG P210, he also drove an Eisenacher Motorenwerk car (likely the final year before Wartburgs). This pretty much tells you that SiG was a weapon of poseur douche even in 1960s Sweden - at least in the minds of the authors of detective novels.

Sig is a VERY high quality gun. Actions are precise and smooth, triggers are great, materials and design are top notch. They've been reliable for Seals, cops, military, etc for a very long time. Since you have interest in Sigs for your own personal reasons, it would make a great first gun. They have multiple trigger options as well.

Two things named sig. Sig pro and sig sauer.

Sig pro is a fine gun. It's pretty much the same as a gloc or a m&p. Plastic bottoms, metal tops flex a lot when fired.

Sig sauer guns are metal on top and bottom. Much stiffer and a fine weapon. Clearly this will make it heavier but much more accurate.

SIG Sauer has a stellar reputation among gun owners and enthusiasts.

I have a SIG Pro 2340 - aka SP2340. It's a .40 cal that has 10+1 in the chamber. Double action/single action and I have loved it.

Easy to use, clean, and very accurate even at longer distances. I recommend it to anyone. (Not that I'm a fan boy of SIG, I'd love to have a glock or kimber, or baretta.)

One thing I hate about SIG is their prices on magazines. $40+ for a 1 magazine kind of sucks.
